title: A reversible patch
description:
Patch bytes in a copy of your own program and be able to undo it exactly.

```
patch at 0x1452: 75 0C -> 90 90 (expected 75 0C: found, applied)
patch at 0x2000: expected 74 10, found 75 10 -> refused (wrong version)
undo -> file identical to the original
```
hints: Check `offset + expected.size() <= file.size()` and `std::equal` the bytes before writing anything (lesson 4.01).
Refusing on a mismatch is what stops a patch from breaking a different build of the program.
requirements: A patch has an offset, the expected original bytes and the new bytes.
Apply only when the original bytes match; record what was there for undo.
Work on a copy, never on the only copy of a file.
stretch: Save patches to a text file and load them back.
